rows.name: LSB_HOSTS
rows.values: Host names, separated by whitespace. The runner keeps the part of each name before the first `.`.
rows.default: Unset: the runner uses only the kernel host name of the server.
rows.effect: The LSF runner (the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server) treats these names as the names of its server. It checks the requested host and the Dice resource totals against them.
rows.notes: The runner adds the kernel host name as one more name. The resource totals are the `dice_numa0` and `dice_numa1` counts that `bhosts` reports. A name that does not match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*` makes both checks fail.

rows.name: LSB_JOBID
rows.values: Text. TRON does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the LSF runner logs `LSF None`. Slice writes no `lsf_job_id` field.
rows.effect: The LSF runner (the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server) writes the value into its log line. `slice bench` and `slice calibrate` write it into the benchmark lock file as `lsf_job_id`.
rows.notes: The benchmark lock file is `.slice-bench.lock`. A Slice process that waits for the lock prints the lock holder with `lsf_job=<value>`. Slice treats an empty value as unset.

rows.name: LSF_ENVDIR
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/dice-lsf-submit`, `bin/dice-lsf-runner` and `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` set it for the LSF commands that they start.
rows.values: Path of the LSF configuration directory. TRON does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: the 3 programs give their LSF commands `/tools/openlava/etc`. Empty: the programs keep the empty value.
rows.effect: The 3 programs pass it to the LSF commands that they start, for example `bsub`, `bjobs` and `bhosts`. They keep a value from the caller.
rows.notes: The programs do not change their own environment. `bin/bsub-build` (the script that submits a remote build to LSF) starts `bsub` with the caller environment and adds no default.

rows.name: LSF_SERVER_HOSTS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/dice-lsf-submit`, `bin/dice-lsf-runner` and `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` remove it for the LSF commands that they start.
rows.values: TRON does not read the value.
rows.effect: The 3 programs remove it from the environment of every LSF command that they start. A value from the shell of the user then has no effect on these commands.
rows.notes: A code comment gives the reason: the installed `lsf.conf` names the LSF server, and an old shell value can name a retired host. `bin/bsub-build` and LSF commands that a user types still get the value.

evidence.quote: # The installed lsf.conf is authoritative. Session exports can outlive an

rows.name: MAKE
rows.values: The command that starts `make`. TRON does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make sets it to the command that started it.
rows.effect: The recipes that start a nested `make` run this command. Examples are the goals `format`, `coverage-report` and `ingest-coverage`.
rows.notes: It is a built-in variable of GNU Make. The makefiles never assign it.

rows.name: MAKECMDGOALS
rows.values: Make goal names, separated by spaces. Slice removes leading and trailing whitespace.
rows.default: Unset: `make` fills it with the goals of its command line. Slice derives no label from it.
rows.effect: The makefile reads the goals while it parses, for example to refuse `make deb` inside the Nix dev shell. It exports the variable to its recipes. Slice then labels its Dice work `make <goals>`.
rows.notes: `DICE_LABEL` and the option `--label` of `slice submit` take priority over it. A value in the environment of `make` replaces the real goals. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` unsets it before it starts `make`.

rows.name: MAKEFLAGS
rows.values: GNU Make flag text. The makefile looks for a `-jN` word, and for the letters `n`, `q` and `B` in the first word.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make builds the value from its command-line options.
rows.effect: The makefile appends `--no-print-directory -j $(NPROC_BUILD)`. For a remote build (a build that `bin/bsub-build` submits to an LSF worker), a `-jN` flag sets `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES` to N.
rows.notes: GNU Make 4.3 shows `-jN` only inside recipes. There the makefile ignores a value equal to `NPROC_BUILD`. A remote build also passes `-B` to the worker. With `-n` or `-q`, the makefile runs `bin/scratch-dir.sh gen` only when `gen` is missing.

rows.name: MAKELEVEL
rows.values: Integer that GNU Make maintains. The makefile compares the text with `0`.
rows.effect: The makefile prints its warning about a run outside the Nix dev shell only when the value is `0`.
rows.notes: The warning also needs empty `IN_NIX_SHELL` and `CI`. GNU Make raises the value by 1 for each nested `make`. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes the variable before it tests the warning. A run with only the goals `deb`, `deb-host` or `gen-deb/...` prints no warning.

evidence.quote: $(warning Running Make outside 'nix develop' is deprecated; this path remains supported during the migration)

rows.name: MAKEOVERRIDES
rows.values: `NAME=value` words. GNU Make fills it with the variable assignments of its command line.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make fills it from its command line. It is empty when the command line has no assignment.
rows.effect: For a remote build (a build that `bin/bsub-build` submits to an LSF worker), the makefile adds these assignments to the `make` command on the worker. It leaves out `REMOTE`, `REMOTE_HOST`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `NPROC_BUILD`.
rows.notes: It is a built-in variable of GNU Make. The makefile never assigns it.

rows.name: MFLAGS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for 4 `make` commands that it starts.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it with `env -u` from the environment of 4 `make` commands. Each of these commands also removes `MAKEFLAGS`, `MAKELEVEL` and `MAKECMDGOALS`.
rows.notes: No file in the repository reads it or gives it a value.

rows.name: NINJA_STATUS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it for Ninja.
rows.values: TRON sets the fixed text `[%f/%t elapsed=%es] `. The text ends with one space.
rows.effect: The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets it for its one `cmake --build` command. Ninja (the build tool that CMake starts) then begins each progress line with this text.
rows.notes: The same command line also sets `TERM=dumb`.

rows.name: NIX_BUILD_CORES
rows.values: Whole number. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` accepts digits only and exits with status 2 on other text. The 2 Python tools parse with `int` and reject values below 1.
rows.default: Unset: 1 job. Empty: the shell readers use 1 job. `export.py` stops with an error. `generate.py` stops with an error when `--jobs` is absent.
rows.effect: Sets the number of parallel jobs in 3 Nix builds: `tron-cmake-test-build` (Ninja jobs), `tron-generated-test-models` (model plugin generation) and `tron-test-model-traces` (model trace export).
rows.notes: The shell readers turn `0` into 1 job. The Ninja build uses at most `NPROC_BUILD` jobs. The 2 Python tools use at most 16 jobs. Their option `--jobs` replaces the variable. `export.py` still parses the variable then.

rows.name: NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE
rows.values: Compiler option text. The check looks for a word that starts with `-frandom-seed=`.
rows.effect: The flake check `cmake-multi-output-hook-contract` (a check that `nix flake check` runs) passes its build step only when the value holds an option that starts with `-frandom-seed=`.
rows.notes: Without that option the check prints `reproducible-build hook did not set a compiler random seed` and fails. No file in the repository assigns the variable.

evidence.quote: 'reproducible-build hook did not set a compiler random seed' >&2

rows.name: NIX_CONFIG
rows.values: Nix configuration text, one setting on each line. The test does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the test starts from empty text.
rows.effect: One test in `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` appends 3 settings to the caller value: `trusted-public-keys`, an empty `builders` and `substitute = false`. It passes the result to the workflow steps that it runs with `bash`.
rows.notes: Only test code uses the variable. The steps come from the job `tron-build` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`.

rows.name: NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it for the Nix build environment.
rows.values: TRON sets the Nix value `true`.
rows.effect: The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets it as a derivation attribute. A comment in the file states the purpose: keep the runtime closures of the test output and the benchmark output independent.
rows.notes: A runtime closure is the set of Nix store paths that an output needs at run time. No file in the repository reads the variable.

evidence.quote: # Keep test and benchmark runtime closures independent.

rows.name: NIX_REMOTE
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets it for the `nix` commands of one test.
rows.values: TRON sets a Nix store address of the form `local?root=<directory>`.
rows.effect: One test sets it to a store below its temporary directory. The `nix` commands of the workflow steps that the test runs then use that store.
rows.notes: Only test code sets it. A comment in the test says that the variable redirects Nix operations.

evidence.quote: # NIX_REMOTE redirects Nix operations, not the consumer shell's symlink

rows.name: NO_COLOR
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/test_install_nix_hooks.py` sets it for the commands that the test starts.
rows.values: TRON sets the fixed text `1`.
rows.effect: The test puts `NO_COLOR=1` into the default environment of the commands that it starts: `git`, `bash` and `lefthook` (the Git hook runner).
rows.notes: Only test code sets it. No file in the repository reads it.

rows.name: NO_PROXY
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. The Python libraries `urllib` and `httpx` read it inside `bin/slice` and `t/proxy/tools/capture.py`. `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` clears it.
rows.values: List of hosts that bypass the proxy. TRON code does not parse it.
rows.effect: 2 tests in `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` remove it or set it to empty text. The proxy address that the tests set then also applies to `127.0.0.1`.
rows.notes: `bin/slice` downloads one vocabulary file with `urllib`. `t/proxy/tools/capture.py` sends its requests with `httpx`. `t/proxy/README.md` says that the replay tests of rinzler_proxy need no `NO_PROXY` entry.

rows.name: OMP_NUM_THREADS
rows.values: Positive integer. `nproc` prints this number in place of the CPU count.
rows.default: Unset: `nproc` prints the number of CPUs that the process may use.
rows.effect: It changes the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs). The makefile takes that default from the output of `nproc` and caps it at 16 jobs.
rows.notes: No file in the repository names this variable. The behaviour comes from `nproc` of GNU coreutils. `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT` caps the number that `nproc` prints. No effect when `NPROC_BUILD` is already defined.

rows.name: OMP_THREAD_LIMIT
rows.values: Positive integer. `nproc` prints at most this number.
rows.default: Unset: `nproc` prints the number of CPUs that the process may use.
rows.effect: It lowers the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs). The makefile takes that default from the output of `nproc` and caps it at 16 jobs.
rows.notes: A makefile comment says that LSF sets it to the number of reserved cores. No effect when `NPROC_BUILD` is already defined. `OMP_NUM_THREADS` also changes the output of `nproc`.

evidence.quote: # Cap concurrency to avoid out-of-memory CI hosts. LSF sets OMP_THREAD_LIMIT
# to the reserved cores, and nproc honors it.

rows.name: OSTYPE
rows.values: Text. The scripts test only whether it starts with `darwin`.
rows.default: Unset: bash sets it to the type of its own operating system. On Linux the scripts take the Linux branch.
rows.effect: With a value that starts with `darwin`, the scripts call `stat` and `chmod` in the macOS form. `bin/update-generated-file.sh` then copies only the mode of the file that it replaces.
rows.notes: On Linux `bin/update-generated-file.sh` copies mode, ownership and extended attributes with `cp`. A value in the environment replaces the value that bash sets. 2 CI test scripts set `OSTYPE=darwin` to run the macOS branch on Linux.

rows.name: PATH
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `dice`, and every script that starts a command by name (`src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp`, `bin/dice`, `config/resource-parser.sh` and 40 more files that name `PATH`)
rows.values: List of directories, separated by `:`.
rows.default: Unset: a Dice daemon in shared mode (one daemon for all users) gives a submitted command the `PATH` of the daemon, or `/usr/bin:/bin`.
rows.effect: TRON programs find the commands that they start by name through it, for example `python3` for the tokenizer script `bin/tokenize_py`. Several scripts put a tool directory first for the commands that they start.
rows.notes: The LSF runner (`bin/dice-lsf-runner`) puts `/tools/openlava/bin` first for its LSF commands. `config/resource-parser.sh` puts the repository `bin` directory first when it holds an executable `yq`. The Dice daemon runs `systemctl` with `/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`. `bin/bsub-build` does not pass `PATH` to the remote job.

rows.name: PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME
rows.values: Path of a Unix socket.
rows.default: Unset: `rinzler-capture.sh` checks `/run/perfetto/traced-consumer.sock` when the directory `/run/perfetto/` exists and is accessible. Otherwise it checks `/tmp/perfetto-consumer`.
rows.effect: `rinzler-capture.sh` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace from a running rinzler) checks this socket before a capture. It stops when a program listens there. It removes an unused socket file that the user owns.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` (a harness that starts its own `traced` daemon and `perfetto` client around one command) does not read the variable. It sets `<socket directory>/consumer.sock` for these 3 programs. `rinzler-capture.sh` also stops when another user owns an unused socket file.

rows.name: PS1
rows.read_by: The shell hook of the Nix dev shell (`flake.nix`)
rows.values: Shell prompt text. The hook replaces each `\u` in it.
rows.default: Unset: the hook sets the prompt to `(nix) ` alone.
rows.effect: On x86_64 Linux, the Nix dev shell hook sets the prompt to `(nix) ` plus the old prompt. It replaces each `\u` in the old prompt with the output of `id -un`.
rows.notes: The hook changes the prompt only when `id -un` prints a name. A comment in `flake.nix` calls this a fix for SSSD (the System Security Services Daemon, a login service for directory accounts).

evidence.quote: # 8. PS1 fix for SSSD (must be last to override .bashrc)

new_terms.definition: `bin/dice-lsf-runner`, the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server. It starts the work through the Dice daemon of that server.
The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker and shows its output. `make` runs it for build goals when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.
A build that `make` sends to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`.
A server that LSF gives remote builds and remote test runs to.
The file `.slice-bench.lock`. `slice bench` and `slice calibrate` hold a lock on it while they update the benchmarks file.
The Dice mode in which one Dice daemon serves all users of a server.
The Nix build that compiles TRON and its tests with CMake. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` defines it.
The build tool that CMake starts to run the compile steps.
A check that `nix flake check` runs. `flake.nix` defines the checks.
The set of Nix store paths that a Nix build output needs at run time.
The Git hook runner. `lefthook.yml` lists the lint commands that it runs before a commit.
The GNU coreutils command that prints the number of CPUs that a process may use.
The Python tokenizer script. rinzler and runtron run it as a child process when they do not use the Rust tokenizer.
The script `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh`. It captures a Perfetto trace from a running rinzler.
The Perfetto daemon that receives trace events from programs over a socket.
The System Security Services Daemon, a login service for directory accounts.

notes: All 24 names are kept. Source was opened for every variable. MAKE, MAKEOVERRIDES and MFLAGS are built-in variables of GNU Make. The makefiles read MAKE and MAKEOVERRIDES as make variables. No TRON code reads them from the process environment. The rows are kept under the rule that an environment value of the same name changes the make variable. GNU Make was probed with a scratch makefile outside the checkout (GNU Make 4.3). A value in the environment replaced MAKE, MAKECMDGOALS, MAKELEVEL and MAKEOVERRIDES. GNU Make replaced an inherited MFLAGS value with its own flags. GNU Make 4.4, the version of the Nix dev shell, was not probed. Only the MAKECMDGOALS row states the replacement, and the unset line of bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh supports it. The default cells of MAKE, MAKEFLAGS, MAKELEVEL and MAKEOVERRIDES describe GNU Make behaviour. No line of the checkout states it. OMP_NUM_THREADS: no file of the checkout names it. The row rests on the behaviour of nproc (GNU coreutils 8.32, probed: 3 gave 3, 40 gave 40, and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=4 capped 40 at 4). For OMP_THREAD_LIMIT the makefile comment states the dependency. Both rows use the group ml-libraries, the group that the task assigns to OpenMP. Their only effect in TRON is the build job count. NO_PROXY: no TRON code reads the name. Two tests remove it or set it to empty text, so tron_use is unsets. The read is inside urllib and httpx. PATH: 42 files of the checkout name PATH as a variable (regular expression search, 3 false matches removed). The read_by cell lists 2 of them and src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp, which uses PATH through popen without naming it. More files use PATH without naming it. NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH: the checkout does not show which Nix component reads it. The input record names the Nix compiler wrapper. The row says only the Nix build environment. NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE: the default cell says only that the check fails. The exact message for an unset variable depends on the shell options of the Nix build. PS1: the default cell follows from bash expansion of an unset variable in the hook line. OSTYPE: the statement that an environment value replaces the bash value was probed with bash 5.1.16. The 2 test scripts that set OSTYPE=darwin depend on it. Two evidence quotes are a part of their source line and not the whole line: GNUmakefile:96 and flake.nix:1996. The whole lines contain the pipe character. The limit of 35 words is applied to every effect cell.
